errata.error: BODC's ERDDAP places three UK National Tide Gauge Network gauges away from where they are. Workington's dataset gives 50.2112, -5.4803, at St Ives in Cornwall, about 500 km from Workington in Cumbria. Immingham's and Newhaven's give -999 for latitude and longitude.
errata.response: The station refresh moves each station to the Environment Agency's position for the same gauge, listed in `POSITIONS` in `src/positions.ts`. An entry applies only while BODC still serves the position it was written against. If BODC moves the station, it keeps BODC's position, and the refresh reports the entry and fails the run until a person checks it.
errata.evidence:
| Station | Dataset | ERDDAP position | EA's position of the gauge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bodc/wor`, Workington | `WOR_ukcff_9310_001` | 50.211182, -5.4803309 | `ea/E73639-anglian`, 54.650691, -3.56717 |
| `bodc/imm`, Immingham | `IMM_ukcff_3751_001` | -999, -999 | `ea/E71124`, 53.63039, -0.18755 |
| `bodc/nha`, Newhaven | `NHA_ukcff_4006_001` | -999, -999 | `ea/E71739`, 50.781775, 0.057004 |

Workington's levels are the Workington gauge's: in November 2025, all 2,786 shared quarter hours of BODC's `ASLVBG02` and the EA's Workington readings are exactly 4.20 m apart (r = 1.0000), which is chart datum's depth below ordnance datum at Workington in NTSLF's table. Immingham's and Newhaven's datasets also give `minTime` as 1970-01-01, a fill value, in `allDatasets`. Checked on 2026-11-09.

errata.error: Times in BODC's UK National Tide Gauge Network datasets on ERDDAP are a few milliseconds off the quarter hour, such as `2024-12-07T07:59:59.998Z` and `2025-01-19T02:44:59.971Z`, up to about 30 ms. The pattern repeats through each day, which suggests the times are stored as fractional days and converted with rounding error.
errata.response: The adapter rounds each time to the nearest minute. It asks for each year with half a minute either side, so a value stamped just before New Year comes with the year it rounds into.
errata.evidence: Lowestoft (`LOW_ukcff_3942_001`) on 1 June 2024 runs `06:00:00.000`, `06:14:59.999`, `06:30:00.001`, `06:45:00.000`, `06:59:59.999`, and so on, with the error growing to 2 ms by the afternoon. Aberdeen's `time_coverage_end` is `2026-09-30T16:59:59.973Z`. The same values in GESLA's copy of BODC's processed files are on whole quarter hours. Checked on 2026-11-09.

errata.error: BODC's ERDDAP datasets for the UK National Tide Gauge Network hold less than its processed files. About one value in 32 is missing, so a 31-day month has 2,880 values, not 2,976. Whole months are missing. Most gauges' records end in December 2024, February 2026 or September 2026, though BODC's processed data page offers the network to August 2026.
errata.response: The lake keeps what ERDDAP serves and leaves the gaps. Monthly's refetch reads every station's last two years again, so months BODC adds later reach the lake. GESLA's `-bodc` records hold BODC's processed files to 2024 or 2025 without these gaps.
errata.evidence:
At Lowestoft (`LOW_ukcff_3942_001`) on 1 June 2024, ERDDAP has 93 of the day's 96 quarter hours. 07:30, 15:15 and 23:00 are missing; GESLA's copy has them (07:30 is 1.956 m). Over May 2024, ERDDAP has no Lowestoft values at all, while GESLA's copy has 2,976.

At Lerwick (`LER_ukcff_4109_001`), the months present have 2,880 values in 31-day months, 2,788 in 30-day ones and 2,602 in February. These months are missing: May to December 2022, October 2023 to February 2024, May 2024, July 2024, and April to September 2025.

Records end on 2024-12-31 at 16 gauges, 2026-02-28 at 9, 2026-09-30 at 15, 2024-12-07 at Mumbles and 2025-11-30 at Workington. Checked on 2026-11-09.

errata.error: BODC's Ilfracombe levels sit 0.9 to 1.6 m off GESLA's CMEMS copy of the gauge on and off from 30 September 2023 to 20 March 2025.
errata.response: 30 September 2023 to 20 March 2025 is flagged `suspect` whole, keeping BODC's own flag as `source_flag`. The lake's QC already flags 82 to 93% of it.
errata.evidence: Found by running GESLA's datum-jump rule (`datumJumps` in `src/sources/gesla`, a 30-day median shift of more than 0.75 m) over every record the lake lists as coastal, and confirmed, November 2026, by daily-mean differences against GESLA's CMEMS copy of the gauge (`gesla/ilfracombe-ilf-gbr-cmems`): the difference is −0.01 m before and −0.02 m after and −0.88 to −1.56 m over the spans.
